# One fresh numbered geometric question; unresolved

Leonid V. Kovalev, *Lipschitz clustering in normed spaces and barycentric spaces*, arXiv:2610.31555v1, Question 6.5, p17: “Is Λn(X) = O(n) for every normed space X?” Here X(n) is the space of nonempty subsets of X of cardinality at most n, with Hausdorff distance, and Λn(X) is the infimum of Lipschitz constants of retractions X(n) -> X(n−1). A retraction fixes EVERY set of cardinality at most n−1. The full question includes infinite-dimensional and incomplete real normed spaces. Complex spaces are regarded as real. The literal weakest reading is: for every X there exists C_X<∞ such that Λn(X)≤C_X n for all n≥2. It does not require convex-hull preservation. Question 6.6 asks the stronger all-target-k bound; it is recorded but not a second fresh slot.

The latest obtained abstract history lists only v1, submitted 22 October 2026 16:59:14 UTC. Actual PDF and HTML obtained; PDF SHA256 a108688020ac249f0367d62a897c8e725b078a6b22f52f19eb59108888e7b134. No DOI or published journal version was authenticated for this source. The AI-use disclosure on p17 is retained. No independent certification of its whole proof is claimed. The global O(n²) source theorem and its special cases are public, not nominations.

Also obtained and read actual predecessor proof bodies: Akofor–Kovalev, *Growth rate of Lipschitz constants for retractions between finite subset spaces*, arXiv:2005.13579v1, 27 May 2020 18:14:14 UTC; journal metadata Studia Math.260(3)(2021)317–326. It supplies Λn≥n−3 and the transfer lemma, not a linear upper bound. Kovalev, *Lipschitz retraction of finite subsets of Hilbert spaces*, latest obtained arXiv:1406.6742v2, 19 April 2015 00:02:25 UTC (v1 26 June 2014 01:08:11 UTC), gives the full gradient-flow proof with bound max(n^(3/2),2n−1). The author listing and newer bibliography differ in their journal-year field (2015 versus 2016); these are retained as metadata, not silently reconciled. Neither actual journal body was obtained. ## Full-quantifier reductions

The per-space and uniform-in-X readings are equivalent for the consecutive question. Suppose no universal constant exists. Choose real normed spaces X_j and integers n_j≥2 with Λn_j(X_j)>j n_j. Form the normed ℓ∞ direct sum Y of the X_j: bounded tuples with supremum norm. The coordinate embedding i_j and projection p_j are contractions with p_j i_j=id. Any retraction on Y(n_j) transfers pointwise to p_j r i_j on X_j(n_j), with no increase in Lipschitz constant. Thus Λn_j(Y)≥Λn_j(X_j)>j n_j. Y cannot satisfy an O(n) bound with one finite constant, contradicting the per-space claim. Conversely, a universal constant plainly gives a constant for each space. Infima need not be attained: apply the transfer to each available retraction and take infima. Completeness is unnecessary. This is a reduction, not a source resolution or a credited theorem.

A sufficient missing operator lemma is precise. For every X,n and positive scale s, seek a permutation-equivariant map T_s:X^n->X^n with (i) a pair at distance ≤s has equal output entries; (ii) max_i||T_s(x)_i−x_i||≤a n s; (iii) when max_i||x_i−x'_i||≤ε, |s−s'|≤2ε, max(s,s')>2ε, outputs differ coordinatewise by at most b n ε. Constants a,b must be universal. Define r(A)=A for |A|<n; otherwise apply T at s=δn(A), the minimum separation, and forget labels. Property (i) reduces cardinality; equivariance makes the map well-defined. If both separations are ≤2ε, the triangle inequality and (ii) bound the output distance by (1+4an)ε. Otherwise the larger separation is >2ε, so nearest-neighbor matching is a bijection of the two n-point sets and |δn(A)−δn(B)|≤2ε. Property (iii) gives bnε. Hence this lemma would solve the full question. The source already supplies (i),(ii), but (iii) currently costs n log n. We have NOT constructed the missing operators.

## Exact failed methods

1. Removing the source averaging step does not keep outputs in X. Take X={(u,v,w) in R³:u+v+w=0}, with the sup norm, and x1=(0,0,0), x2=(2,0,−2), x3=(0,4,−4). The minimum separation is s=2. Source scalar proximal map P_t minimizes 1/2 sum(u_i−a_i)²+t sum_{i<j}|u_i−u_j|; apply P_1 coordinatewise. In coordinate 1 the data (0,2,0) fuse to (2/3,2/3,2/3); in coordinate 2, (0,0,4) become (1,1,2); coordinate 3, (0,−2,−4), becomes (−2,−2,−2). Thus the three output sums are −1/3,−1/3,2/3: none lies in X. These exact minimizers follow from the sorted isotonic formula and satisfy convex directional optimality (also checked independently). The collision succeeds, but there is no valid retraction into X. This does not prove that a different embedding or map fails.

2. Hard closest-pair merging is discontinuous. On the real line compare Aε={0,2,4+ε} and Bε={0,2,4−ε}, 0<ε<1/2. Their distance is 2ε. The unique closest pair in Aε is {0,2}, and in Bε is {2,4−ε}. Replacing that pair by its midpoint gives {1,4+ε} and {0,3−ε/2}; output distance is 1+3ε/2. The ratio diverges as ε->0. No tie-breaking convention repairs this one-sided discontinuity. This defeats that rule, not Question 6.5.

3. The logarithm is forced in a specific radial-weight estimate. Suppose φ≥0 is absolutely continuous on [c,b], φ(b)=0, φ(c)≥n, and |φ'|≤L(φ+1) almost everywhere. Then log(1+φ) is absolutely continuous, with derivative of absolute value ≤L. Integrating gives log(n+1)≤L(b−c). In the source c=(n−1)/2, b=(3n−1)/2, so b−c=n and L≥log(n+1)/n. The source exponential φ(r)=(exp(λ(b−r))−1)_+, λ=log(n+1)/n, attains this lower bound. Thus replacing λ by C/n with fixed C cannot satisfy all THESE hypotheses for unbounded n. This is not a lower bound for every weighting scheme, every source-map Lipschitz constant, or Λn itself. A more geometric cancellation estimate could still remove the logarithm; the source total-variation argument need not be sharp.

## Complete applicable classical/source bridge and its precise limit

There IS a full linear bridge for absolute λ-Lipschitz retracts, already public in source Corollary6.3. Embed a nonempty metric X into ℓ∞(X) by i(x)(z)=d(x,z)−d(o,z). Boundedness follows from the triangle inequality; equality in the isometry follows by choosing z=x. The absolute-retract hypothesis gives p:ℓ∞(X)->i(X) with Lip(p)≤λ and p restricted to i(X) the identity. Source Theorem2.3 supplies R:ℓ∞(X)(n)->ℓ∞(X)(n−1) with Lip(R)≤2n−1. Pointwise p∘R∘i fixes every smaller set, has at most n−1 points, and has constant ≤λ(2n−1). Every hypothesis is accounted for. This covers ℓ∞ and other absolute retracts; it supplies no dimension-independent p for an arbitrary normed space. A scalar McShane extension extends scalar functions, not an X-valued retraction. Hilbert gradient flow uses inner-product monotonicity and yields n^(3/2), still insufficient. No complete classical bridge was found for ALL normed spaces, and no routine/shortness-based exclusion is asserted.

540 exact rational proximal-pair controls, 2,880 finite directional checks and the exact subspace/instability witnesses pass. They do not establish the universal missing lemma, refute arbitrary retractions, or resolve either source question. No PROOF.md is supplied because there is no complete ordinary candidate. Honest result: one fresh unresolved precise question, zero nominations and zero credit.

# r193: regular triangle maximizers, full-scope question unresolved

## Primary statement and chronology

Actual primary read: Pablo Romero and Louis Petingi, *Trace-minimal graphs maximizing the number of spanning trees*, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.36127, v1, Conjecture 10 on p5 and the complete proof of Lemma25/Proposition26 on pp7–8. Definitions and surrounding related-work statements pp1–6, final applications and bibliography pp13–15 inspected. Abs https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36127 lists only v1, submitted 26 October 2026 18:35:32 UTC. PDF SHA256 3e4d28a0da96775b89a8610e3553d6ad8d61bb7b8e7a9f9417c1411967110875. The PDF says a preliminary version appeared in LAGOS2025, Procedia Computer Science273(2025)177–184, with different title *Construction of infinitely many trace-minimal graphs with maximum number of spanning trees*. That publication body is unread; no journal-version equivalence asserted. The source attributes Conjecture10 to Petingi–Rodríguez, Discrete Math244(2002)351–373, *A new technique for the characterization of graphs with a maximum number of spanning trees*. It cites Gong–Yang–Wang–Chen, Discrete Math349(2026)114936, as proving degrees1–5. Those two bodies and Ábrego et al2006, LAA412:161–221, remain unread. No DOI is authenticated. Author/institutional routes returned404 or certificate failure; no TLS disabling or publisher bypass attempted.

For every finite simple d-regular G0 on n vertices minimizing the number ν of induced three-vertex paths among ALL d-regular graphs on n vertices, and every integer p≥1, G0 disjoint-union p copies of K_(d+1) must be ν-min among all d-regular graphs on n+p(d+1) vertices. Conversely every ν-min G' at that larger order must be isomorphic to H disjoint-union pK_(d+1), for some d-regular H of order n. The converse then forces H to be optimal by additivity. No connectedness, large-order, degree≤5 or trace-minimal restriction is imposed. We retain both directions and all feasible d,n,p; d=0 is trivial. The primary's Proposition26 covers only d≥3,n≥d³, not all source orders.

This is ONE fresh investigated question, zero ordinary resolutions. Saegusa Conjecture23 and the quiver height conjecture are not additional selected slots. No old Bonnet/r186 counting/r191 automorphism question reopened.

## Exact all-order reduction

Let T_d(N) be the maximum number of triangles in a d-regular graph of order N whenever that class is nonempty. Each wedge (two incident edges) is either the unique central wedge of an induced P3 or one of the three wedges of a triangle. Therefore

    ν(G)=N binom(d,2)−3τ(G).

The primary's extracted Remark11 notation is visually ambiguous, but the wedge coefficient is binom(d_i,2), not d_i²; the direct counting above fixes its meaning without changing the extremizers. ν-min and triangle-max are equivalent on regular classes.

The FULL conjecture is equivalent to this universal clique-forcing statement:

    For every d≥0 and every feasible N≥2(d+1), EVERY
    triangle-maximizer in R_d(N) has a K_(d+1) component.  (CF)

Conjecture⇒CF: choose n=N−(d+1). Then n≥d+1, and nd is even because Nd and d(d+1) are even. A simple regular graph on n exists: for even d join each cyclic vertex to offsets±1,...,±d/2; for odd d, n is even, use offsets±1,...,±(d−1)/2 and the opposite perfect matching. Thus one can choose optimal G0 at n and invoke the converse with p=1.

CF⇒conjecture: a triangle maximizer at n+d+1 contains K_(d+1); deleting it leaves an optimizer at n, since any improvement of the remainder improves the original. Hence T_d(n+d+1)=T_d(n)+binom(d+1,3), and EVERY maximizer has the required form. Repeat at n+i(d+1) for i=p,...,1: all orders at which CF is used are≥2(d+1), since the original feasible n≥d+1. This proves both source directions. Isomorphism and all multiplicities are preserved. The reduction is routine, not the missing theorem.

This changes the research task to a structural extremal lemma, rather than falsely replacing the converse by a single example. A plausible universal route is degree-preserving switching that strictly increases triangles whenever a clique-free extremizer has N≥2(d+1). The source supplies such a local-optimality consequence only strong enough for its large-order comparison, not this global switching theorem.

## Why the strongest read proof does not close CF

Read complete closest proof: Lemma25 and Proposition26 in the latest source. The argument uses the quoted Ábrego local bound: in a triangle-maximizer having no clique component, every neighborhood is missing at least two pairs, so ν≥2N. Write N=q(d+1)+r,0≤r≤d. A competitor consists of (q−1) cliques plus a feasible d-regular residual graph H on s=d+1+r vertices. Discarding even the nonnegative residual triangle contribution shows it suffices that

    2N > s binom(d,2).

The source uses N≥d³ as a convenient sufficient bound. Exact residual triangles can improve this but do not uniformly force the desired inequality. For example d=20,N=53,r=11,s=32: take complement Hbar to be K16,16 with five disjoint perfect matchings removed, so Hbar is11-regular and triangle-free; H is20-regular. Inclusion–exclusion on triples gives τ(H)=binom(32,3)−176·30+32·binom(11,2)=1440. H∪K21 has2770 triangles and ν=1760. The local bound ν≥106 for a hypothetical clique-free optimizer is far too weak to exclude it. These numbers are not evidence such an optimizer exists, or that H∪K21 is globally optimal. They isolate the exact insufficiency of the comparison method.

Moreover the local bound requires GLOBAL extremality. Take two K4s, delete01 and45 and add04 and15. This is a connected3-regular graph on8 vertices with four triangles and no K4 component. Its eight neighborhood deficits are four1s and four2s. Thus the tempting assertion that every clique-free regular graph has each local deficit≥2 is false. The graph is not a source counterexample: two disjoint K4s have eight triangles. This is an exact method countermodel only.

The complete applicable classical adaptation has therefore been exposed: wedge counting, clique additivity, deletion induction and the source's neighborhood-gap/competitor argument prove the conditional reduction and large-order range. They do NOT prove CF at all degrees/orders. No complete classical theorem read subsumes the full endpoint. We do not exclude the question by shortness or by use of classical tools. Full missing bridge: prove CF uniformly for all feasible d,N≥2(d+1), or produce an exact extremal clique-free witness with certified global optimality. A graph with many triangles alone does not refute the forward direction or certify the converse.

# Exact target and source boundary

For every finite field F, every integer m>=2 and every ring R with identity,
if the simple graphs Gamma(R) and Gamma(M_m(F)) are isomorphic, must the rings
be isomorphic? Gamma has vertices R minus its center; distinct vertices are
adjacent iff they commute. No assumed finiteness, F-algebra structure,
semisimplicity or field center is added to R. This is the literal full
Conjecture1.1 on p1 of Hamid and Vahid Shahverdi, arXiv:2610.37150v1.
The complete four-page body, including centralizer/normalizer proofs and
radical/double-centralizer argument, was read. Latest abs lists v1 only,
27Oct2026 12:49:21UTC, no journal reference. Original2004 attribution is
reported by this primary, not independently authenticated from that body.

Public Theorem1.2 settles every even m. Remark3.1 already gives conditional
transfer from any prime size to its multiples. Its bibliography reports
Dorbidi–Manaviyat2024 settles m3 assuming Z(R) is a field. The actual2024
publisher full/PDF routes returned403 and are unread. No claim that its
proof has been inspected or that it is the latest worldwide result. Search

# Strongest complete available classical-adaptation bridge

The following is a conditional source adaptation, not a new nominee.
Assume recognition holds for size k>=2 over EVERY finite field; put m=kn,
n>1. Also use the order/center determination theorem cited by the source:
|R|=q^(m²), |Z(R)|=q. These cited upstream results are dependencies, not
independently reproved here. A companion block Q of an irreducible polynomial
of degree n repeated k times has matrix centralizer M_k(F_(q^n)). A graph
isomorphism transfers its noncentral closed-neighborhood centralizer graph;
by the assumed recognition its counterpart C in R is that simple ring.
Its field center contains Z(R); hence Z(R) is a finite domain, thus F_q.

Let J=J(R). C intersect J=0: it is a proper ideal of simple C since1 notin J.
If u in1+J normalizes C, then ucu^-1-c is in C intersect J for all c in C,
so u centralizes C, hence the defining element x of C=C_R(x). Thus u in C
and u-1 in C intersect J, forcing u=1. The action on all such centralizers
is free. The corresponding matrix centralizers are one conjugacy orbit
with normalizer GL_k(q^n) semidirect Gal(F_(q^n)/F_q). Therefore |J| divides
|GL_(kn)(q)|/(n |GL_k(q^n)|). If q=p^ell, its p-valuation is
ell*k²*n*(n-1)/2-v_p(n); hence dim_F J < m²/2.

The commutator map j -> jx-xj on J has zero kernel and is bijective. It
follows by subtracting a suitable j that the image of C is exactly

The remaining prime-base recognition must recover enough ring structure
from a graph to force semisimplicity and the correct field center at odd
prime size. Merely choosing an irreducible degree-m matrix centralizer gives
a commutative field on the matrix side, whose own commuting graph is empty.

J={(0,0,U)} has order16, square zero, and quotient F2 x M2(F2) semisimple,

For every integer n>2 and real random variables X,Y with E|X|^(n−1),E|Y|^(n−1)<infinity on an atomless probability space, the conjecture is

    X ≤_(n-wcx) Y iff there is Z in L^(n−1)
    with X ≤_((n−1)-cx) Z ≤_(n-cx) Y.

Write C_j(W,t)=E[(W−t)_+^j]/j!. Weak n-convex order means equality of moments 1,...,n−2 and C_(n−1)(X,t)≤C_(n−1)(Y,t) for EVERY real t. Full n-convex order additionally requires equality of moment n−1. Thus Z must match X,Y through moment n−2 and match Y at moment n−1. No boundedness, nonnegative support, density, finite-support or n=3 restriction is permitted. The n=3 case is the source's public Theorem 4.1, not a fresh target. ## Exact all-order obstacle formulation

Set p=n−2, D(t)=C_(p+1)(Y,t)−C_(p+1)(X,t) and Δ=(E[Y^(p+1)]−E[X^(p+1)])/(p+1)!. Equal lower moments and dominated tail estimates give D(−infinity)=Δ and D(+infinity)=0. Weak order gives D≥0, hence Δ≥0.

The missing construction is equivalent to finding an integrable h≥0 such that

    integral_R h = Δ;
    integral_t^infinity h ≤ D(t) for every t;
    C_p(X,.)+h = C_p(Z,.) for a probability law Z in L^(p+1)
    having the common moments through p.

Necessity: take h=C_p(Z)−C_p(X). The first order gives nonnegativity; Proposition 2.2's moment identity gives its integral Δ; Tonelli applied to each positive-part transform gives the tail identity C_(p+1)(Z)−C_(p+1)(X)=integral_t^infinity h. The terminal order is precisely the upper obstacle. Conversely these three requirements give the first order, the terminal transform inequality and, by the same moment identity, the last moment equality. This accounts for ALL n, t, moment and integrability conditions; it does not construct h. If Δ=0, h=0 and Z=X already work, so the substantive existence problem is Δ>0.

The last requirement is essential: for p≥2 a valid C_p is C^(p−1); distributionally (−1)^(p+1) times its (p+1)-st derivative is a positive probability measure, with the appropriate left polynomial and right vanishing boundary behavior. Finite moment p+1 is an additional tail condition. Merely finding a nonnegative mass allocation below D does not guarantee these derivative and boundary constraints. For instance the running infimum H(t)=inf_(s≤t)D(s) has the right monotonicity for a survival mass profile, but differentiating it may give atoms or a function that fails the transform conditions. No theorem repairing this uniformly is supplied.

## Exact source-admissible obstruction to max-gluing

Let X be equally likely ±1 and let Y take −2,0,2 with probabilities 1/8,3/4,1/8. Both laws have moments (mean,second,third)=(0,1,0). Define unnormalized Q_j(W,t)=E[(W−t)_+^j]. For a=|t|,

    Q_3(Y,t)−Q_3(X,t) = 0                          if a≥2,
                         (2−a)^3/8                 if 1≤a≤2,
                         (4−6a²+3a³)/8              if 0≤a≤1.

Direct expansion proves the formula on t≥0; symmetry and equal cubic polynomials extend it to negative t. The last polynomial decreases from 4 to 1 on [0,1], since its derivative is −12a+9a²≤0. Hence X≤_(4-cx)Y, in particular this pair satisfies the full weak-order hypotheses at n=4.

Nevertheless max(Q_2(X,.),Q_2(Y,.)) is not Q_2 of ANY probability distribution. At zero the two functions equal 1/2. Their derivative difference is 1/2; consequently X dominates immediately to the left, Y to the right. The maximum has left derivative −1 and right derivative −1/2. Every Q_2 transform of an L² law is continuously differentiable with derivative −2E[(W−t)_+], by dominated convergence. This corner is impossible. Translating both laws by 2 also gives a nonnegative-support example. It defeats direct max-gluing even on source-admissible data; it does NOT refute Conjecture 5.1. Here Δ=0 and Z=X is a valid separator. The source's order-three proof uses ordinary convex call transforms, where corners are allowed; the higher regularity obstruction is specific to extending that mechanism.

An additional exact method barrier concerns stationary excess inversion. For nonnegative W with 0<EW<infinity its stationary-excess density is P(W>t)/EW on t≥0, necessarily nonincreasing. Uniform[1,2] has density 0 then 1 then 0 and cannot be such an image. Distributional inversion would put negative mass at 1 and positive mass at 2. Thus an ordinary separation theorem applied to transformed variables cannot simply be inverted without proving the separator lies in the transform's image. This is a complete range obstruction, not a claim that the unread 2014 body uses precisely this invalid step.

## Classical adaptation challenge and unresolved universal step

The complete applicable classical implication is the easy direction. If X≤_((n−1)-cx)Z, integrate its nonnegative C_(n−2) difference from t to infinity to obtain C_(n−1)(X)≤C_(n−1)(Z). Combining with Z≤_(n-cx)Y and the common moments through n−2 gives X≤_(n-wcx)Y. Finite L^(n−1) moments justify the integrals. This proves sufficiency, not necessity. The source's entire n=3 necessity proof was read early; it uses convexity, maximum/chord construction, a continuous area parameter and a single-crossing endpoint argument. The explicit corner above prevents treating those same operations as valid higher transforms without a new construction.

Translation is a full bridge from a nonnegative separation theorem to any COMMON bounded-below pair: expand (W+a)^k binomially to preserve all required moment equalities, and use C_j(W+a,t)=C_j(W,t−a); translate the resulting Z back. It does not cover arbitrary left-unbounded laws. An approximation extension needs order-preserving approximants with exact lower moments and enough tail control to retain moment n−1 of the separators. Plain clipping need not preserve these conditions. A bounded highest moment alone does not supply that control: μ_R=(1−R^(−q))δ_0+R^(−q)δ_R converges weakly to δ_0 but has q-th absolute moment 1 for every R, while each lower positive moment is R^(j−q)→0. These laws are a precise compactness-method warning, NOT feasible separators for a claimed counterexample. No complete all-order classical bridge is obtained, so there is no shortness-based exclusion.
